assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only three-days-of-happiness:shinbashi@original-novel#novel-monograph (the canonical v1.0 Shinbashi novel monograph, qualified COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY (bounded) with standalone self-containment PASS and sampled primary-source fidelity PASS and no material correction, according to the discovery row) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the single Japanese witness TDH-JP-01; its close evidence is Ch14 P0010-P0077, with the Ch15 reunion used only as a comparison from which Shinbashi is absent. The monograph's marker do_not_use_as_literary_evidence and its statement that it is a literary portrait, not a behavioral reconstruction, were read as method inputs, as were the completion audit's original gate-2 row (minor figures, one to three scenes, no differentiated portrait), its later bounded qualification and its statement that no reconstruction operation is authorized. The readings, the longitudinal notebook, the synthesis, the audit and the Kusunoki, Miyagi, Himeno and substitute-watcher monographs are not cited, and nothing is borrowed from them. No translation, adaptation or other edition is assessed, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Ch14 P0010-P0077 of TDH-JP-01: the pub intervention (P0010-P0043), the same-night gathering (P0046-P0065) and the car loan a few days later with his revised explanation (P0069-P0077). His earlier disturbed look when he saw Kusunoki talking to Miyagi is Kusunoki's recollection, without a locator in the monograph. assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph centers Shinbashi on acting before belief is settled. His own account (Ch14 P0022-P0032) is that he takes Kusunoki's conduct as a performance meant to unsettle others' perceptions, that it has partly worked on him, and that he wants to see what happens if he actively accepts the sense of someone there; he denies both literal belief and a wish to help. The car loan away from any audience (P0069-P0077) and his hope for broader acceptance (P0033-P0043) count against a spectacle-only reading. Not D: this is one chapter, and the monograph states that the mix of curiosity, experiment and generosity at the pub remains unknown, so it cannot tell which motive decides a choice; that is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. E is the floor and stands on a self-stated motive and its revision.

One located change for Shinbashi: from the performance hypothesis at the pub (Ch14 P0022-P0032) to the conditional view at the loan that mime no longer explains what he has felt (P0069-P0077), with no new visual testimony. The earlier discomfort is Kusunoki's recollection. Not D: there is no development across more than a few days, and his later state and judgment are not narrated.

Shinbashi's register is sampled in three scenes: polite forms carrying a coercive request to the harasser, respectful address to Kusunoki and Miyagi, repeated hedging and marking of conjecture, and a pronoun shift from boku to ore at the loan and back to boku in his reflection (Ch14 P0010-P0018, P0022-P0043, P0072-P0075). The monograph itself says the sample cannot establish his speech outside this circle or a stable rule for choosing pronouns. Not D: no phase or addressee system beyond these exchanges.

Two located ordinary acts by Shinbashi: inviting Kusunoki and Miyagi to share leftover drinks with his friends before he goes home (Ch14 P0046-P0065) and tossing Kusunoki his car keys for a period when he will not need the car (P0069-P0077). Not D: no routine, home life or recurring habit is shown.

Shinbashi is shown toward Kusunoki (from a neighbor's discomfort, as Kusunoki remembers it, to a practical ally), toward Miyagi only through Kusunoki's mediation (the greeting with a supplied reply, the relayed handshake and thanks, Ch14 P0010-P0043), toward the harasser once, and beside friends whose responses the monograph attributes to them, not to him. Not D: each relation is a single episode, and what would change his conduct toward any of them is not established.

Shinbashi's inner state reaches the page only through his spoken self-account and Kusunoki's record: his experimental question, the report that Kusunoki's description matches the person he had imagined, and the vague sense that she would thank him (Ch14 P0022-P0043). The monograph keeps these as his reports, not as observation. Not D: no other access.

One conflict case: Shinbashi defuses the pub harassment by public acquaintance, a formally polite but, in Kusunoki's hearing, intimidating request for a harasser's seat, and size; no fight is recorded, and his public smile drops once the men leave (Ch14 P0010-P0021). Not D: a single case, with Kusunoki's attribution of the harasser's change to Shinbashi's size and look.
The monograph records Shinbashi's acts of help and his denial of a rescue motive but no ethical reasoning or weighing; nothing is graded from that silence.

The monograph calls the gathering hospitable and theatrical, but it attributes the play (Suzumi's suggestion, Asakura's test, Riko's demand) to Shinbashi's friends; Shinbashi only looks on expectantly. His own humor is not characterized, so nothing is graded.

The monograph covers every passage in which Shinbashi acts (Ch14 P0010-P0077) and names his absence from the Ch15 reunion; its locators route to notebook IDs (TDH-C063, C066, C071; TDH-S076) and readings U14-U15, and the discovery row records standalone and sampled primary-source fidelity checks that passed without material correction. Not B: the portrait is short, its fidelity check was sampled, and the remembered earlier sightings carry no locator. Not D: his complete presence in the novel is covered and checked.

The evidence affirmatively bounds Shinbashi: he never claims to see Miyagi; he denies both literal belief and a helping motive at the pub (Ch14 P0022-P0032); his failed conversational alignment shows he cannot perceive her (P0010-P0021); the handshake is mediated, so neither touch perception nor direct conversation is attested (P0033-P0043); he calls his own social prediction groundless; and he is not present at the Ch15 reunion, which therefore cannot confirm his perception. Not B: few situations. Not D: these are located denials and contrary conduct, not only silence.

Shinbashi's three scenes are anchored by paragraph (Ch14 P0010-P0043, P0046-P0065, P0069-P0077) with relative timing (the same night, a few days later). Not B: one short span with relative dates. Not D: an explicit, anchored sequence.

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph states that Shinbashi's sample cannot establish his speech outside this circle or a stable pronoun rule, and his exchanges with Miyagi are mediated. Illustrative lines beyond the three located exchanges would be underdetermined.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Ch14 P0010-P0077 only: the pub intervention, the same-night gathering and the car loan a few days later; nothing after Ch14 P0077.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Kusunoki as his neighbor, Miyagi only through Kusunoki's mediation, the pub harasser once, and his friends Suzumi, Asakura and Riko as the gathering's company.
setting_constraints: The novel's world before the Ch15 reunion, with Miyagi imperceptible to Shinbashi
The pub, his gathering and his door as located; no home life, work or other setting
No primary-source reading beyond the cited monograph

scenario_readiness.note: Shinbashi's evidence is one chapter, and the motive mix that would decide his conduct in a new situation is explicitly unknown. A novel scenario can only be checked against the located pub, gathering and loan.
One gathering and one loan are located; Shinbashi's social life beyond them, including with his friends, is not characterized beyond that night.
No ethical reasoning by Shinbashi is recorded.
Nothing about Shinbashi's romantic life is recorded.
Shinbashi's occupation or work conduct is not recorded.

known_limits.statement: Shinbashi acts only in Ch14 P0010-P0077 (three scenes over a few days); his life elsewhere, his family history and his response to either final sale are not given.

The exact mix of curiosity, experiment and generosity behind Shinbashi's pub intervention is unknown; he denies a helping motive, and his friends' enjoyment supports a spectacle reading that the later car loan counts against.

Shinbashi never claims to see Miyagi; his greeting, handshake and exchange of thanks with her are mediated by Kusunoki, and his reports of matching and anticipating her are his reports, not observations.
Shinbashi is not shown at the Ch15 reunion, where others describe seeing Miyagi, so it cannot confirm what he perceived earlier or tell his eventual judgment.
Shinbashi's pronoun choice shifts between boku and ore within the sample, and the monograph states it cannot establish a stable rule or his speech outside this circle.
The cited evidence contains no reconstruction model, probe or evaluation of Shinbashi; the monograph describes itself as a literary portrait, not a behavioral reconstruction.
